meta.title: MCPClient — the Kernel
meta.description: Exposes a live Minecraft 1.8.9 client to LLMs over MCP: observe, act on, hot-swap and deeply debug the running game — with every call gated by a 7-layer, NT-style privilege kernel.

hero.title: MCPClient
hero.slogan: Turn a live Minecraft JVM into a programmable substrate an AI can reach — with kernel-debugger-grade control.
hero.intro: A -javaagent injects a running Minecraft 1.8.9 client and hands the full capability spectrum — observe, act, hot-swap, deep-debug — to an LLM over the Model Context Protocol. Every single call must pass through the same 7-layer, NT-style privilege kernel.

what.title: What is this
what.body: MCPClient (codename: the Kernel) is a system-level control platform. It turns a Minecraft client that is actually rendering into a fully controllable, programmable substrate. Exposing that control to an LLM is the most important entry point — but not the essence. The essence is total system-level control over a live JVM; an AI is simply its flagship way to drive it.

security.title: 7-Layer Security Kernel
security.subtitle: Modeled on the Windows NT privilege system; all layers AND together — any one denial denies the call.
security.note: A single decision authority: SeReferenceMonitor.evaluate(), with IoManager.supervise() as its only call site. The HTTP front door goes through the same supervised handler and cannot bypass it.

capabilities.title: Capability Packs C1–C9
capabilities.subtitle: The full spectrum, from introspection to debugger-grade execution control

modules.title: Module Architecture
modules.subtitle: A three-tier structure. The test: remove it, and can the rest of the spine still compile and run on its own?
